subject: Sizing proposal — FalconPoint onboarding: model footprints, KV buffer, and quant tradeoffs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@falconpoint.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@falconpoint.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing proposal — FalconPoint onboarding: model footprints, KV buffer, and quant tradeoffs

Hi Amit / Priya —

Thanks for the call this morning. As promised, attached is a concise sizing worksheet with our recommended Dedicated capacity options based on the two model families you mentioned (LongForm-L14 / Compact-34B) and your 30k-32k context target. A few high-level observations up front: 

- Context length dominates GPU memory for autoregressive workloads because of the KV buffer. For simulations we ran, a 32k prefix adds a roughly linear memory cost that can exceed the model weights for large models.
- Quantization (4-bit vs 8-bit vs int8 dynamic) trades off quality for model resident memory. For Compact-34B we can move from an 80GB GPU requirement down to a 48GB class GPU for serving if we accept 4-bit qlora-style weights + activation strategies, but that increases CPU/host-side preprocessing and has a small latency cost on cold starts.
- For LongForm-L14 (34B variant) our recommendation for predictable tail-latency is dual H100-80GB for the primary pool with warm 48GB fallback nodes for lower-cost bursts.

Attached: FP_model_memory_estimates.xlsx (per-model breakdown, KV buffer assumptions, per-token KV bytes, and per-GPU packing options) and a short Redwood Dedicated options PDF.

Ask: Can you confirm the expected 95th percentile RTP (real-time prompt) token length on your side? We used 14k tokens as the baseline in the sheet but the deal economics change significantly if your 95th jumps >20k.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the 95th percentile token length and peak concurrent sessions (or target QPS) so we can finalize fleet counts.
- If you'd like, Marcus (cc'd) can run a short capture with a ~100-session synthetic replay to validate latency with the proposed 4-bit and 8-bit profiles.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Sizing proposal — FalconPoint onboarding: model footprints, KV buffer, and quant tradeoffs

Vanessa / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the worksheet. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) 95th pct token length: our analytics team reports 95th ~18k tokens currently (lots of long-document summarization jobs). We do have ~30% of requests shorter (<2k).
2) Concurrent sessions: peak expected is ~180 concurrent interactive sessions for our pilot (QPS ~30 sustained during peaks).
3) Quality constraints: we cannot accept noticeable regression on multi-hop instructions; Priya is the technical lead on evals and will flag anything that drops end-to-end label accuracy >1.5% on our internal eval suite.

Given the >15k 95th, please highlight where we should expect the biggest bill jumps (KV buffer vs model resident memory). Also, can you confirm that the 4-bit option will still allow retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with 8k context windows for the embedding/recall path?

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Product, FalconPoint
amit@falconpoint.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@falconpoint.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@falconpoint.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing proposal — FalconPoint onboarding: model footprints, KV buffer, and quant tradeoffs

Amit / Priya —

Appreciate the specifics — that 18k 95th materially changes node counts but we can skew the fleet mix to control cost while preserving latency SLOs. A few technical clarifications I pushed into the worksheet (see tab "pack-options") and summarize below: 

- KV buffer math (high level): we assume KV entries stored in 16-bit for key/value by default (~4 bytes per value vector element when using float16); per-token KV for LongForm-L14 at our layer sizes is ~1.2MB per 1k tokens (i.e., ~21.6MB for 18k). That scales linearly. For 32k you'd hit ~38MB per request in KV memory. This is per inflight request — so concurrent requests multiply this cost.

- Resident weights vs KV: For Compact-34B in fp16 the model weights alone are ~68GB; 8-bit or int8 quant drops resident to ~42GB; 4-bit QAT-style pushes us to <=28GB but requires per-batch dequant steps and slightly higher CPU/GPU kernel overhead. So with 4-bit we can place Compact-34B on 48GB GPUs (1 model per GPU with small KV headroom) and pack 2 smaller low-latency replicas on 80GB nodes for heavy prefix workloads.

- RAG / retrieval considerations: embedding/recall path is orthogonal — you can keep your FAISS/ANN layer at normal sizes. When retrieving 8k windows and concatenating to prompt, the KV buffer only cares about the total token sequence served into the model. If you send retrieval separately to a smaller-context model for rerank, you can save KV overhead. In short: 4-bit weight quant doesn't stop RAG, but large retrieved windows increase KV memory linearly.

- Fleet recommendation (pilot):
  • Primary pool: 6 x H100-80GB (reserved) — handles warm/long-context tails with headroom for autoscaling.
  • Secondary: 10 x 48GB A6000-class nodes (or equivalent) for low-precision 4-bit packed replicas — lower cost for steady throughput.
  • Autoscale policy: prefer warm spill to the 48GB pool for throughput; set a hard cap fallback to our hosted small-model tiers for non-critical requests.

- Cost/pricing note: we provided two committed tiers in the attached PDF (Monthly reserved vs Annual). The bigger lever is how often you need >12k prefixes concurrently — we can granularize the commitment around percentile windows (e.g., reserving a certain number of 95th-percentile slots).

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical run on Thu where we replay a 100-session trace? I can bring a small script that emulates KV growth and measures tail latency with the two quant profiles.

- Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Sizing proposal — FalconPoint onboarding: model footprints, KV buffer, and quant tradeoffs

Marcus / Vanessa —

This looks good and aligns with our internal estimates. A couple of follow-ups before we commit: 

- Eval tolerance: we will run a 48-hour A/B sweep. If the 4-bit profile passes (<=1.5% delta), we will sign up for the lower-cost secondary pool. If it fails, we will want more 80GB reserved capacity.
- PO and procurement: finance needs the committed monthly numbers and the net terms (30 vs 45). Can you send the committed-tier pricing for the two fleet mixes (H100-heavy + 48GB-lean) as a line item?
- Replay: Thu 11:00 PT works for a 30-min session. Marcus — please send the replay script and any pre-reqs.

We attached a simple procurement timeline in our response to the HubSpot deal record. Looking forward to the replay.

Best,
Priya Rao
Technical Lead, ML Infrastructure, FalconPoint
priya.rao@falconpoint.ai
